# Lotería de los Pueblos

Canonical site: https://app.loteria.to/

Lotería de los Pueblos is a free, no-account picture-lotería game for phones, classrooms and families. It has 144 illustrated cards. Every card has a Spanish and English name and synthetic call. The original 54 cards also have Nahuatl, Yucatec Maya and Cusco-Collao Quechua names and synthetic calls. The Indigenous-language names are legacy entries based on references that remain unverified; they have not been confirmed by native-speaker review and are not presented as community-approved. The added 90 cards do not have Indigenous-language names or calls.

## Play online

[Open the home page](https://app.loteria.to/). One person creates and hosts a room; 1–19 others join from their phones using a link, QR code or five-character room code. A room supports 2–20 people. Each player chooses an app language (Spanish or English) and a spoken language independently. The room uses the cards available in all selected spoken languages: Spanish and English cover 144 cards, while the three existing Indigenous-language options cover the original 54. Cards are called automatically in shuffled order at the host's chosen pace. Players identify the called word from written choices and mark the matching picture on their board.

## Public pages and route facts

- [Home](https://app.loteria.to/): create or join a phone-based room; explains the language coverage and links to the other modes.
- [Deck](https://app.loteria.to/deck): browse and filter all 144 cards by category. Spanish and English names appear across the full deck; the legacy Indigenous-language names appear on the first 54 original cards. Individual cards can be linked with fragments such as `https://app.loteria.to/deck#card-jaguar` (the fragment is `card-` followed by that card's ID).
- [Solo](https://app.loteria.to/solo): play offline against 1–3 computer players, with selectable difficulty, call speed and spoken language.
- [Print](https://app.loteria.to/print): generate printable PDF boards for paper play. Available card coverage follows the selected spoken language: 144 for Spanish and English, 54 for Nahuatl, Yucatec Maya and Quechua. Paper play uses physical markers and a caller; it is a separate mode from an online room.
- [Credits](https://app.loteria.to/creditos): source of truth for content notes, artwork, audio, fonts, software and contributor credits.

Private room and host URLs are not public reference pages: `/host`, `/r/{code}` and `/ui`. The room API is under `/api/`.

## Content, audio and licences

Spanish and English names were written by the project team. The legacy Nahuatl, Yucatec Maya and Quechua names include drafts based on dictionary and grammar references that have not all been verified; they have not been confirmed by native speakers. Nahuatl spelling is Classical/Central while its synthetic voice is Huasteca (`nhe`).

Spanish and English audio use Kokoro-82M under Apache-2.0. Nahuatl, Yucatec Maya and Quechua audio use Meta MMS-TTS under CC BY-NC 4.0, requiring attribution and non-commercial use. See [Credits](https://app.loteria.to/creditos) for the full current credits and licence notes, including artwork, typefaces and software. These audio terms do not establish licences for every other project asset.
